title: A Cubic Tinkertoy-like Heterometallic Cluster with a Record Magnetocaloric Effect

synthesis.procedure: Ni(OAc)2·4H2O (0.5 mmol), GdCl3·6H2O (0.6 mmol), and H2HEIDA (0.25 mmol) were added to 7 mL of acetonitrile/water (5:2 by volume) and stirred for 0.5 h. Triethylamine (225 µL) was added, followed by another 0.5 h of stirring. The mixture was transferred to a Teflon-lined reactor and held at 160 °C for 1.5 days. Cooling to room temperature at 15 °C h−1 afforded yellow blocky crystals.
synthesis.temperature: 160 °C; cooled at 15 °C h−1 to room temperature
synthesis.time: 0.5 h stirring before and after base addition; 1.5 days heating
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cooling to room temperature yielded yellow blocky crystals.

properties.summary: The cluster shows predominantly antiferromagnetic interactions and a large magnetocaloric effect. Its reported maximum isothermal magnetic entropy change was 52.65 J kg−1 K−1 from magnetization data at 2.5 K for a 7 T field change.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The cubic cluster cation has a Tinkertoy-like inorganic core described as 15 interpenetrating shells of Platonic and Archimedean polyhedra. The article also describes its assembly geometrically from six trumpet-like faces joined by vertex blocks.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the supporting information's Gd152Ni14@Cl24 procedure, replacing GdCl3·6H2O with SmCl3·6H2O: Ni(OAc)2·4H2O (0.5 mmol), SmCl3·6H2O (0.6 mmol), and H2HEIDA (0.25 mmol) were stirred in 7 mL of acetonitrile/water (5:2 by volume) for 0.5 h. Triethylamine (225 µL) was added and the mixture stirred for another 0.5 h, then heated in a Teflon-lined reactor at 160 °C for 1.5 days. Cooling to room temperature at 15 °C h−1 afforded yellow blocky crystals.
